title: Why long requests pile up
predict: Some requests take a second and some take an hour. Which algorithm keeps one server from drowning?
caption: Round robin keeps dealing long requests onto a server that is already busy; least connections sends them to a free one. Under high variance, use least connections.

title: Nine seconds of errors
predict: A backend dies one second after the last poll. With a 10-second poll, for how long do users see errors?
caption: With polling, LB servers route to a dead backend from stale config until the next poll. Pushing the change at once closes the window.

title: A lock outlives its holder's time
predict: Consumer 1's job takes six minutes; its lock expires after five. What happens when it finally releases?
caption: The lock expires, consumer 2 takes it, and a blind delete by consumer 1 removes consumer 2's lock. Release only if it's still yours, in one atomic step.

title: Winning a majority
predict: Two clients race for one lock on five nodes. One gets three, the other two. What must the second one do now?
caption: Three of five, in time, wins the lock; the loser releases what it took and retries after a random delay. Distributing the lock buys fault tolerance, not speed.
